title: Abdali Reorders Sirhind and Misjudges the Khalsa

blocks.text: The page continues Abdali's redistribution of power after the Delhi settlement. Must he turn out the Singhs from Punjab is the governing demand placed upon his dependents, for then alone would he be able to collect revenues and restore Afghan authority in the region.

To support that program, did Abdali invite Amar Singh and draw him into the circle of reward and obligation. He conferred the title of a Raja in hopes that local authority, prestige, and Sirhind's administration could be used to steady the frontier against Sikh pressure.

Yet the narrative undercuts Abdali's confidence. Little did he realise the power of the Khalsa Panth, for while he distributes titles and offices, the Sikhs are already gathering strength and preparing a far more unified resistance than his camp expects.
